correctness.rationale: The incidence model has exactly 21 flags and its canonical representatives are uniquely normalized at the three point-zero flags. Every proper four-colouring appears exactly once by pointwise injections, every acyclic colouring passes exactly the six bichromatic forest tests, and exactly one canonical representative exists per S4 orbit because any acyclic colouring must use all four colours. Independent edge-prefix and point-injection programs both enumerate 119784 acyclic orbits and the exact 599760 directed legal moves. Exhaustive BFS independently gives 392 singleton, 112 order-14, 24 order-42, one order-40040 and one order-76776 component. The stated class-size condition for frozen states follows from exhaustive class-size enumeration. All finite certificates were compiled and executed. The mathematical assertion is finite; no infinite generalization or uncomputed global diameter is asserted.

Neither vertex colouring of the same incidence graph nor ordinary proper edge-colouring of a different graph contains a reduction yielding this finite classified graph.

originality.rationale: Acyclic edge-colouring optimality (four colours) is standard and explicitly excluded from the novelty assertion. The checked general existence papers and list-edge recolouring results do not state the exact Heawood palette-orbit census or its acyclicity-constrained local move components. The full published closest same-graph strong-edge-colouring result has seven colour classes each an induced matching and whole-class trades, so neither it nor its stronger exact reconfiguration statement implies this different four-colour/all-bichromatic-forest single-edge graph. Search of named and numeric aliases found no exact covering table. Originality is assessed to best knowledge only, subject to the listed unread full-text and historical database risks.

value.rationale: The known acyclic chromatic index four only proves existence, while the new result classifies the entire 119784-state palette-unlabelled optimum configuration space and identifies a surprising mix of 392 frozen states, 136 nontrivial small components and two huge noncommunicating sectors. It answers the natural mobility question for all valid optimal acyclic edge-colourings of the canonical 14-vertex cubic incidence graph; the state count, sharp component distribution and frozen-profile condition are not routine relabelings of the known index. A finite exact classification is intrinsically useful for edge-colouring reconfiguration and frozen-state comparisons.
